topic: Template Metaprogramming with Type Traits and Compile-Time Computation
explanation: Template metaprogramming in C++ allows compile-time computation and type introspection, enabling developers to write generic, efficient, and type-safe code. Using templates, type traits, and constexpr functions, C++ programmers can perform calculations, enforce constraints, and select implementations during compilation, which enhances performance and correctness. This approach is fundamental in modern C++ for creating flexible libraries like the Standard Template Library (STL) and for implementing advanced generic programming techniques.

example_explanation: This example demonstrates template metaprogramming by defining a compile-time function 'gcd' to compute the greatest common divisor, and a type trait 'IsIntegralType' to inspect types at compile time. The 'process' function uses SFINAE (Substitution Failure Is Not An Error) with 'enable_if' to only compile when the template argument is an integral type. The static_assert verifies the correctness of the compile-time GCD calculation. Overall, this showcases how C++ templates enable powerful compile-time logic, type safety, and generic programming in modern C++.
